one_sentence: IMF Working Paper WP/25/48 (Feb 2025), "Monetary Policy and Inflation Expectations: High-Frequency Evidence from Brazil" by Carlos Gonçalves, Mauro Rodrigues and Fernando Genta, uses Rigobon-style heteroskedasticity identification on daily Brazilian data to show monetary tightening lowers inflation expectations and appreciates the exchange rate.

issues.reason: Cross-checked against the IMF eLibrary listing (journals/001/2025/048), IDEAS/RePEc (RePEc:imf:imfwpa:2025/048), EconPapers, SSRN (abstract_id=5166242), the NEP-CBA report (2025-04-28), and the title page of the official IMF PDF itself (wpiea2025048-print-pdf.pdf, fetched via proxy). All five independent sources agree: WP/25/48 (= Volume 2025, Issue 048) IS this exact title with these exact three authors, in this order. The bib entry is not a mixed-up citation; number, title and author list are all internally consistent and correct. Author spelling/accents also confirmed exactly as given: 'Carlos Gonçalves' (with the cedilla-ç and til-a) appears on the PDF title page itself, not just an ASCII-stripped RePEc rendering.

Bare numeric month (as a literal string '2') is nonstandard BibTeX hygiene; the conventional form is the three-letter BibTeX month macro (jan..dec) or a spelled-out string, which most .bst styles render correctly and abbreviate as needed. Content-wise the value is right: the paper's IMF publication date is 2025-02-28 (confirmed via IMF eLibrary/IDEAS/NEP-CBA and the 'Authorized for distribution ... in February 2025' line on the PDF itself), so month should read February/feb, not merely the digit 2.

No url or doi field was present in the entry. The IMF eLibrary does not appear to assign this working paper a DOI (none listed on the eLibrary abstract page or the PDF itself), so a doi field cannot be added in good faith. Adding the canonical IMF publications-page URL gives a durable, verifiable anchor; the direct PDF (https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2025/english/wpiea2025048-print-pdf.pdf) and SSRN mirror (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5166242) are secondary confirmations of the same document.
